# Flashcard Infographic — Design

**Goal:** Let a deck's flashcards be turned into an infographic — a title plus a handful of icon-and-bullet sections summarizing the material — generated by the same Claude integration this app already uses to draft cards and write test questions. Reachable from Deck Manager once the deck has cards.

**Scope in one line:** any number of saved infographics per deck, each generated on demand at one of three detail levels, from either every card or a chosen subset, rendered through a layout this app owns and controls — not arbitrary HTML the model writes.

## Decisions (confirmed 2026-09-13, revised same day after mockup review)

| Question | Decision | Why |
|---|---|---|
| How the model's output becomes the visual | The model returns **structured JSON** (a title, several sections, each an icon + heading + bullet points); the app renders it through **one fixed layout/CSS we design**, never the model's own markup | This app has never rendered arbitrary HTML from anywhere (no `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`, no iframe) — every AI response so far is structured JSON a typed component renders (cards, quiz questions). Letting the model emit real HTML/CSS would need iframe sandboxing and would make every deck's infographic look inconsistent. |
| Icon choice | The model picks from a **fixed enum** of icon names given to it in the prompt; nothing freeform | The app can only render icons it has SVGs for. A closed vocabulary means there is never an icon name that has to fall back silently. |
| Where the infographic is shown | A **dedicated route**, `/deck/:id/infographic`, phase-driven like `/deck/:id/test` | Consistent with Study and Test already being their own screens rather than modals; an infographic benefits from full-screen room the way a test does. |
| Which cards feed it | Either **every card**, or a **chosen subset** picked from a checklist before generating | The user's own call: default to simplicity (all cards) but don't force it. |
| How much detail | A choice of **Basic / Standard / Detailed** at generation time, each giving the model soft guidance on how many sections/points to write (and so, indirectly, how many printed pages the result reads as) — **never a strict page-count rule**, just a target | The user's own requirement: length should be steerable per-generation, not fixed, and the model should never be held to an exact page count — pages are a side effect of content volume, not a target the prompt enforces directly. |
| Longest an infographic may run | **Up to 5 pages'** worth of content**, as a soft ceiling** the Detailed level's clamping enforces at parse time — not something the model is told as a rule | Same reasoning: the cap exists so a single generation can't run away in size, but it is enforced by clamping the parsed response, not by instructing the model to count pages (which it cannot do reliably, since it never sees how its own text will lay out). |
| One infographic per deck, or many | **Many.** Each deck can hold any number of saved infographics, listed on their own screen | The user's own call, made once mockups made "one, overwritten on regenerate" feel wrong in practice: different detail levels and different card subsets are legitimately different, worth keeping side by side rather than each replacing the last. |
| AI gating | Same `AiSettings` (`off` / `hosted` / `byok`) already used for cards and quiz — the setup screen shows the same "turn on the AI helper" panel when it's off | One AI on/off switch for the whole app, not a second one for this feature. |
| Cost confirmation | **None** beyond the "Generate infographic" button itself | Matches "Write missing questions" and card drafting: an explicit button press is already the confirmation. |
| Export / download | **Out of scope for v1.** Raised and explicitly declined twice in the same conversation — once outright, once again after weighing HTML-file vs. PDF-library tradeoffs | Recorded as a deliberate, twice-considered cut, not an oversight — the natural place to revisit is once a user actually asks for it. |

## Mockup

Three of the four screens below (Setup, the infographics list, View) plus the Deck Manager entry point were mocked up in the app's real visual language (tokens, type, existing component patterns — no new visual language) and approved before this spec was finalized. The structure below matches that mockup; it is the source of truth for layout, not a separate description invented afterward.

## Data model

`src/types.ts` — four new exports, alongside the existing `Deck`/`Folder`/`Flashcard`:

```ts
/**
 * The icons an infographic section can carry. Fixed on purpose: the app can
 * only render icons it ships its own SVG for, so the model is given exactly
 * this list in the prompt and never asked to invent a name.
 */
export type InfographicIcon =
  | 'book' | 'lightbulb' | 'brain' | 'chart' | 'list'
  | 'arrows' | 'target' | 'clock' | 'check' | 'warning'
  | 'network' | 'question';

/**
 * How much content to ask for. A prompt-shaping choice, not a stored render
 * setting the view screen reads — but it's kept on the record because the
 * infographics list shows it (see the mockup's "Standard" / "Basic" tags).
 */
export type InfographicDetail = 'basic' | 'standard' | 'detailed';

export interface InfographicSection {
  heading: string;
  icon: InfographicIcon;
  points: string[];
}

/**
 * One saved infographic. A deck can have any number of these — different
 * detail levels or card subsets are different infographics, not versions of
 * one, so there is no "the deck's infographic" singular and no overwrite.
 */
export interface Infographic {
  id: string;
  deckId: string;
  title: string;
  detail: InfographicDetail;
  sections: InfographicSection[];
  /** Which cards this one was built from, for the list screen's "N cards" line. */
  cardIds: string[];
  createdAt: number;
}

/**
 * What the model's response actually contains — title and sections only.
 * `Infographic` adds `id`, `deckId`, `detail`, `cardIds` and `createdAt`,
 * none of which are in the model's own reply (it never sees a deck id or an
 * id of its own, and doesn't need to). Same split `LlmCard` (cardPrompt.ts)
 * already keeps from the stored `Flashcard`.
 */
export interface LlmInfographic {
  title: string;
  sections: InfographicSection[];
}
```

### Per-level guidance and clamps

The prompt tells the model a *target* range for the chosen level; the parser then *clamps* — never rejects — to a wider ceiling, so an unusually thorough or terse reply still gets stored rather than thrown away for missing a soft target:

| Level | Target sections | Target points/section | Clamp ceiling (sections) | Clamp ceiling (points/section) | Reads as roughly |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Basic | 3–4 | 2–3 | 5 | 4 | ~1 page |
| Standard | 5–7 | 3–4 | 8 | 5 | ~2 pages |
| Detailed | 8–12 | 3–5 | 14 | 6 | up to 5 pages |

These numbers are the "soft ceiling" mentioned in the Decisions table: at Detailed's clamp (14 sections × 6 points), a reply is generously long but still bounded — the model is never told "stop at 5 pages" because it cannot judge its own layout, but the app never stores something wildly larger than the level implies either.

## Storage: `src/db/db.ts`

- `DB_VERSION` goes from `3` to `4`. The upgrade adds an `if (oldVersion < 4)` block that creates an `infographics` object store with `keyPath: 'id'` and a `by-deckId` index — the same shape `flashcards` and `testQuestions` already use, now that a deck can hold more than one. The `oldVersion < 1/2/3` blocks do not change.
- New functions:
  - `getInfographicsForDeck(deckId: string): Promise<Infographic[]>` — `getAllFromIndex('infographics', 'by-deckId', deckId)`, sorted newest first (matches the library's own "Newest" default, and is what the list screen shows).
  - `saveInfographic(infographic: Infographic): Promise<void>` — a `put` keyed by `id`, so generating another one never touches an existing row.
  - `deleteInfographic(id: string): Promise<void>` — one `delete`, called from both the list screen's "Delete" and the view screen's "Delete this infographic."
- `deleteDeck` (`src/db/db.ts:266`) adds `'infographics'` to its transaction's store list and to the existing cursor-loop over `by-deckId` indexes (the loop already there for `flashcards`/`testQuestions` — `infographics` joins that same `for (const store of [...])` array, since a deck can now own more than one row here too).

## Generation: prompt, transport, and the server

Follows the existing `cards` / `quiz` / `vignette` / `ocr` task pattern exactly — a new task name, `'infographic'`, touching the same handful of places those already do:

- **`src/lib/infographicPrompt.ts`** (new). Same shape as `quizPrompt.ts`: the system prompt text plus its response parser, nothing else, and — like every file in this family — **no runtime import of the DOM, `localStorage`, or anything else browser-only**, since the Netlify function imports it directly into the server bundle.
  - `INFOGRAPHIC_SYSTEM_PROMPTS: Record<InfographicDetail, string>` — one prompt per level, not one shared prompt (see below for why). Each instructs the model: given some flashcards (front/back/context) and a chosen level (Basic/Standard/Detailed, with that level's target section/point counts spelled out — see the table above), write one infographic as JSON (`{ title, sections: [{ heading, icon, points }] }`); `icon` from the exact list of `InfographicIcon` values; headings and points short enough to read at a glance; no restating a card's back verbatim as a bullet — synthesize, don't transcribe. The prompt states the target as guidance ("aim for roughly N sections"), never as a hard page or section cap.
  - `parseInfographicResponse(text: string, deckName: string, detail: InfographicDetail): LlmInfographic | null` — the model replies with one JSON **object** (`{ title, sections }`), not the JSON array `parseJsonArray` (`textUtils.ts:214`) is built for, so this parser reuses only `stripJsonFence` (`textUtils.ts:147`, format-agnostic) and then does its own `{`…`}` slice + `JSON.parse` — the object-shaped equivalent of what `parseJsonArray` already does for arrays. Then **clamps rather than rejects**, using the ceiling for the given `detail` level from the table above: sections beyond the ceiling are dropped from the end; points beyond a section's ceiling are dropped from the end; an unrecognized `icon` value falls back to `'list'`; a missing/empty `title` falls back to `deckName`. Returns `null` only when the response isn't parseable JSON at all or has zero usable sections — mirroring how `parseCardsResponse`/`parseQuizResponse` already treat a genuinely unusable response as "nothing," not a thrown error.
- **Why three prompts/tasks instead of one prompt reading a `detail` field from the payload:** `generateHandler.ts`'s request validator requires every task's payload to be a plain array (`Expected a non-empty "sections" array`), so an object payload like `{ detail, cards }` would be rejected by hosted mode before ever reaching the model. `detail` instead selects *which task* is called — matching how `vignette` and `vignette-audit` are already separate tasks rather than one task with a mode flag.
- **`src/lib/aiTransport.ts`** — add `'infographic-basic' | 'infographic-standard' | 'infographic-detailed'` to the `AiTask` union, each level's prompt to the client-side `PROMPTS` map (used only in `byok` mode, which has no server to ask), and `MAX_TOKENS` entries of `4000` for all three — sized for the Detailed level's ceiling (14 sections × 6 points of short text, plus JSON structure, comes to roughly 2000 tokens by rough character count; 4000 leaves the same kind of headroom `quiz`'s 8000 leaves over its own typical batch, per this file's existing comment on why headroom here is "close to free").
- **`src/server/generateHandler.ts`** — the same two additions (`MAX_TOKENS`, `PROMPTS`) for all three task names, importing `INFOGRAPHIC_SYSTEM_PROMPTS` from the same `src/lib/infographicPrompt.ts`, exactly as this file already does for the other four prompts.
- **`src/lib/infographicGenerator.ts`** (new, mirrors `quizGenerator.ts`'s role, not its batching — this task is a single request, no retry batches): exports `generateInfographic(deckId: string, deckName: string, cards: Flashcard[], detail: InfographicDetail, settings: AiSettings, signal?: AbortSignal): Promise<Infographic>`. Trims each card to `{ front, back, context }` the way `quizGenerator.ts` already trims cards before sending them (the payload is a plain array of these, nothing else — `detail` doesn't ride along in it, see above), looks up which `AiTask` that `detail` maps to, and calls `callModel(task, payload, settings, signal)` (matching `callModel`'s real signature — `task, payload, settings, signal?, images?` — in `src/lib/aiTransport.ts:267`), parses the reply with `parseInfographicResponse(text, deckName, detail)`, and assembles the full stored shape — `{ id: crypto.randomUUID(), deckId, title: parsed.title, detail, sections: parsed.sections, cardIds: cards.map(c => c.id), createdAt: Date.now() }` — throwing when parsing returned `null`. It does **not** call `saveInfographic` itself — `InfographicMode` does that after a successful call, keeping "generate" and "persist" as separate steps the way the rest of the app already does.

## UI/UX flow

Four screens, matching the approved mockup:

- **`src/components/DeckManager.tsx`** gets one more button in `.manager-actions`, next to "Study this deck" / "Test this deck": **"Create infographic"**, `disabled={cards.length === 0}` (same guard the other two already use), calling a new `onInfographic(deckId)` prop.
- **`src/routes/router.tsx`** adds `{ path: 'deck/:deckId/infographic', element: <InfographicRoute /> }`.
- **`src/routes/DeckRoute.tsx`** wires `onInfographic={(id) => navigate(\`/deck/${id}/infographic\`)}`.
- **`src/routes/InfographicRoute.tsx`** (new) — reads `deckId` from the params, renders `InfographicMode`, wires `onExit={() => navigate('/')}` (matching Study/Test's own `onExit`; the top-bar's history-aware Back button, not this per-screen exit, is what already handles "return to wherever you came from" generically).
- **`src/components/InfographicMode.tsx`** (new) — the phase owner, `'list' | 'setup' | 'generating' | 'view' | 'error'`. On mount, reads `getInfographicsForDeck(deckId)`: any existing rows open into **List**; none, straight into **Setup** (an empty list screen would be a wasted click for a deck's first infographic).
  - **List** (`src/components/infographic/InfographicList.tsx`, new) — one card per saved infographic: its title, a detail-level tag (Basic/Standard/Detailed), section count, which cards it used ("all 24 cards" or "9 cards"), and its date. "View" opens it in **View**; "Delete" asks `confirm('Delete "<title>"? This can't be undone.')` (matching `deckActions.ts:15`'s existing deck-delete confirm — a plain `confirm()`, not a custom modal, since this is a cheaper, easily-regenerated action than deleting a deck) and, if confirmed, removes it (`deleteInfographic`) and stays on **List**. Always at least one tile: a dashed "+ Create infographic" opens **Setup** — with zero saved infographics left (the last one just deleted, say), that tile is the only thing on the grid, which reads as the empty state without needing one specially built.
  - **Setup** (`src/components/infographic/InfographicSetup.tsx`, new) — "How much detail?": three cards, Basic / Standard / Detailed, each with its one-line description and rough page estimate from the table above (**Standard** pre-selected by default); "Which cards?": the existing-pattern choice between "All cards" and "Choose cards", the latter opening a checklist styled like the existing "+ Add decks" list (`DeckLibrary.tsx:409`, `.add-decks-list`) — one row per card, its front text as the label, a checkbox. Shows the same `AiSettingsPanel` gate `QuizSetup` already shows when `ai.mode === 'off'`. A "Generate infographic" button, disabled until at least one card is selected in "Choose cards" mode.
  - **Generating** — a simple loading state, matching `QuizGenerating`'s look.
  - **View** (`src/components/infographic/InfographicView.tsx`, new) — the title, then each section as a small card: icon, heading, bullet list, with a visible dashed page-break divider between logical page groups (a purely presentational cue — see "Pagination is presentation, not data" below). Two actions: "Back to infographics" (→ **List**) and "Delete this infographic" (the same `confirm()` as **List**'s Delete, then `deleteInfographic` and → **List**). No "Regenerate" — making another one is "+ Create infographic" from **List**, since there is no longer a single infographic a regenerate would replace.
  - **Error** — the same "here's what went wrong, try again" notice shape `QuizSetup`'s failed-generation state already uses.
- **`src/components/infographic/icons.tsx`** (new) — one small inline SVG per `InfographicIcon` value, in this app's existing icon style (24×24 viewBox, `stroke="currentColor"`, 2px stroke, round caps/joins).

### Pagination is presentation, not data

`Infographic.sections` is a flat list — there is no `pages` field, and the model is never asked to decide where a page break falls. "Up to 5 pages" is a size guideline the Basic/Standard/Detailed clamps enforce (see the table above); *where* a page actually breaks is a rendering concern for **View**, not something stored. This keeps the data model simple and keeps a future export (out of scope here, but the obvious next feature) free to choose its own pagination — e.g. print CSS `break-inside: avoid` per section — without needing to agree with what was stored at generation time.

## What does not change

- Every other "Back to library" / exit control in the app (`StudyMode`, `QuizSetup`, the top bar) — untouched.
- No new AI mode, no new settings surface beyond the existing `AiSettingsPanel`.
- `getAllDecks()` / the library screen's read pattern — unaffected, since infographics live in their own store.

No staleness tracking: unlike test questions (which compare a stored `cardHash` to detect an edited card), a saved infographic carries no signal that the cards it was built from have since changed — it simply reflects whatever they said at generation time. Generating another one (at any detail level, from any card subset) is how you get something current. Worth calling out as a deliberate v1 cut, the same way export/download is, rather than an oversight.

## Verification

- `parseInfographicResponse` is a pure function (no DOM, no network) — covered by a `tools/test-infographic.mjs` script in this repo's existing style (`tools/test-quiz.mjs` is the closest precedent: parser/clamping checks always run with no key; a second part that calls the real model only runs when one is set). Cases worth naming explicitly for the plan: clamping at each of the three levels' ceilings (too many sections, too many points), an unrecognized icon falling back to `'list'`, a missing title falling back to `deckName`, and a genuinely unparseable reply returning `null`.
- The IndexedDB additions (`getInfographicsForDeck`, `saveInfographic`, `deleteInfographic`, the extended `deleteDeck` cleanup, the v3→v4 upgrade) are checked the way this repo already checks browser-only storage code with no headless-browser runner available: manually, against the running dev server — the same category of check the back-navigation feature's own spec used for its browser-only behavior. Worth specifically checking that a deck with two infographics at different detail levels only loses the deleted one, not both, when "Delete" is used from **List**.
